findings: The account's graph-level routing premise is substantially supported: Java selects DotSplines.ORTHO from linetype, DotStringFactory serializes splines=ortho and forcelabels=true, vendored Graphviz dispatches EDGETYPE_ORTHO only under ORTHO, and Rust now sets that same graph-level mode from the effective linetype.
No fixture/family-keyed router selection or fresh-evidence keyed logic was found in the implementation diff. The old ER route-delta shim is removed.
Acceptance is nevertheless rejected by fresh valid held-outs: five of six perturbations fail strict no-oracle comparison. Failures span ordinary Class, nested packages, and ER crow-foot/nested cases.

The common unresolved mechanism is label placement under ORTHO. Java emits center labels through Graphviz xlabel and recovers the label position from Graphviz's solved SVG, while Rust still suppresses center labels in the graph and synthesizes positions from the shortened route midpoint plus ORTHO_XLABEL_VERTICAL_INSET.
The passing last-spline control supports case-insensitive/last-declaration linetype precedence, but it does not rescue the mechanism because the ORTHO held-outs fail.
Build portability was not recompiled by this review per instruction. The existing binary and Java references were sufficient for the requested evidence; no Cargo or rustc process was invoked.
verdict_reason: REJECTED. Effective linetype alone appears to activate the real graph-level orthogonal router, and removing the old ER path deltas is directionally generative, but the implementation is not acceptable because Rust still models ORTHO center labels with a synthetic midpoint heuristic instead of Java's Graphviz xlabel channel. Fresh ordinary Class, nested package, and ER crow-foot perturbations fail, so the mechanism has not survived held-out adversarial validation.
